root_cause.text: fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:fsctl_set_sparse() changed a file’s sparse attribute via xattr without enforcing either the share-level writable flag or the opened handle’s write/attribute access rights, causing a permission bypass in ksmbd FSCTL handling.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit state that “FSCTL_SET_SPARSE in fsctl_set_sparse() modifies the file's sparse attribute and saves it through xattr without any permission checks,” and the patch adds the previously missing checks `test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE)` and `fp->daccess & (FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE | FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add write-permission and file-access checks to fsctl_set_sparse() so sparse attribute changes are denied with -EACCES when the share or handle is not writable.
intent_record.what: The change adds two access-control checks to fsctl_set_sparse(): an early check that the tree connection has KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE and returns -EACCES with a debug message if not, and a post-file-lookup check that the opened file descriptor's daccess includes either FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE, otherwise setting ret to -EACCES and jumping to the existing out path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now refuses sparse-file attribute changes when the share is not writable or when the caller's file handle lacks sufficient write-related access rights, preventing unauthorized execution of the sparse-setting operation and returning an access-denied error instead.

grouping_result.intent: Add write-permission and file-access checks to fsctl_set_sparse() so sparse attribute changes are denied with -EACCES when the share or handle is not writable.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by adding the missing share-level writability and handle access checks in fsctl_set_sparse(), preventing unauthorized sparse attribute modification.

candidates.rationale: This line shows fsctl_set_sparse() proceeding directly to manipulate sparse-related file attributes after only looking up the file handle, with no preceding enforcement of share writability or handle write/attribute access rights. It is the closest available pre-fix statement in the hunk embodying the unauthorized attribute-change path.

This statement reflects that the function moved on to filesystem/xattr operations once a file pointer was found, without any access-control check in between. It helps identify the vulnerable flow where attribute changes were prepared despite missing permission validation.

The function only validated that a file descriptor existed. The root cause is that this lookup was not followed by checks for share-level writability or the opened handle's write/attribute rights before sparse attribute modification proceeded.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is where fsctl_set_sparse() proceeds into sparse attribute manipulation after merely obtaining the file pointer, without first enforcing share-level writability or checking that the opened handle has write or attribute-update access. That missing authorization gate is the permission-bypass root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it fully shows the logic that changes the sparse attribute and whether any permission checks are performed. The vulnerable construct is present: after looking up the file descriptor (`fp = ksmbd_lookup_fd_fast(work, id);`), the code immediately modifies the file attributes based solely on `sparse->SetSparse` (`fp->f_ci->m_fattr |= ATTR_SPARSE_FILE_LE;` / `fp->f_ci->m_fattr &= ~ATTR_SPARSE_FILE_LE;`). If the value changed and DOS attrs are stored, it writes the updated attribute to xattr via `ksmbd_vfs_set_dos_attrib_xattr(...)` at line 7497. There is no check anywhere in this function for share-level writability or for the opened handle having write or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES-style access rights before performing the update. Since the root cause is exactly that `fsctl_set_sparse()` changed the sparse attribute via xattr without enforcing share writable flag or handle write/attribute permissions, this function contains the bug. The fix is not present because no guarding condition or access validation exists before mutating `m_fattr` and calling the xattr setter.
